editorial:
Imagine if you could pay to see exactly how your life ends or who you marry. That is the wild setup here, where a guy dealing with a huge loss finds a place called a Time Spa. It feels like a high-end clinic, but instead of massages, they sell you a peek into your own future. You get to follow this man as he tries to find some peace, but he quickly realizes that knowing what happens next is actually a nightmare. The vibe is kind of quiet and mysterious, making you feel the same confusion and worry that the main character feels as he digs deeper into the secrets of the spa.

The acting is solid and keeps you grounded while the plot gets weird. The pacing starts slow to build the mystery, but the twists in the second half really pick up. While some parts might feel a bit too slow for people who want non-stop action, the emotional payoff is great. It is a great pick for a rainy night when you want something to think about.
endingExplained: You find out that the Time Spa does not actually show the future, but instead creates a fake version of it to control people. The man discovers that his visions were manipulated to keep him paying for more sessions. In the end, he chooses to stop looking at the fake future and accepts his grief. He leaves the spa behind, realizing that living in the present is the only way to actually heal.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about time travel and human emotions.
similarMovies: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
